review.note: The one-time task release is 0.19.0. No catalog-to-Komga mapping or remote Komga behavior was changed. Forty focused installed-metadata, version-boundary and CLI cases passed on SQLite; eight matching read-only startup/previous-schema/refusal cases passed on live disposable MariaDB. The fresh installed-wheel smoke checked runtime dependency metadata, origins, CLI help and a real schema10 SQLite read-only catalog open. No live Komga service or remote PATCH was used. Reviewed every direct build, runtime, optional/development and Node candidate against the previous committed receipt, including candidates outside the new bounds. Registry discovery at checked_at reports h2hdb 0.45.9; that schema-9 release is deliberately excluded. The explicitly supplied Core 0.46.0 candidate wheel SHA256 970d14a6188e5f20a62a8fdfd5bddf20a30d139faba923a63c48d48b41b1d571 was reviewed with Core runtime/schema commit 11cf659: schema 10 retains immutable consumption attempts, recovers only an exact expired current ingest generation, keeps old-token fencing and allows the next download after completion. Public facade/receipt call shapes remain unchanged; database compatibility is breaking and requires the Core-provided offline schema-9-to-10 converter. The supported range is >=0.46.0,<0.47.0, rejecting every prior schema lane and the unverified next lane without a runtime shim. Normal uv resolution in a fresh Python 3.14 venv installed the explicit consumer and Core wheels with all development extras; pip check passed. Actual installed versions, direct wheel origins, runtime bytes and METADATA were checked against both artifacts. Ruff 0.17.0 official notes (https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/releases/tag/0.17.0) change implicit defaults; explicit py314 target and configured rules remain authoritative. Mypy 2.4.0 (https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html) was exercised by the unmodified strict fast gate. Testcontainers 4.15.0 (https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-python/releases/tag/testcontainers-v4.15.0) adds the CrateDB module and preserves the tested disposable MariaDB use. All other unchanged candidate versions retain the prior upstream review evidence. The new complete fast gate passed without rule relaxation. These checks do not claim index-backed deployment, full merge review, the automatic release gate, complete deep matrices, live accounts or production validation. No push, publish or deployment was performed.
